# Historical evidence synthesis: Scene RSI v2.1, r1

## Scope and evidence matrix

This is an audit-only synthesis of batch 1 of 1, covering all 10 inventoried trajectory files, S0224–S0233. The supplied audit reports cover all explicit chunks, but the underlying reference and rendered image pixels are not available for independent inspection here. Line citations below refer to the original `trajectory.jsonl` paths identified by source ID; the common path prefix is `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r1/`.

| Source and original path after prefix | Observed attempt and validation | Outcome boundary |
|---|---|---|
| **S0224** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/test/commons_189918915/trajectory.jsonl` | Initial warehouse-interpreted build rendered; student diagnosed color and composition issues, then executed a nonempty revision. Both steps were selected (lines 3–12); final review returned `DONE` (lines 14–15). | Two technical render successes; visual fidelity and improvement unknown. |
| **S0225** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/test/commons_80372956/trajectory.jsonl` | Ceiling/chandelier-interpreted build rendered; student diagnosed spoke orientation, framing and brass appearance and executed changes. Second render selected; `DONE` (lines 3–15). | Technical success, not an independently verified visual match. |
| **S0226** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl` | Café-interpreted build rendered; student revised camera, furniture, foliage and lights after comparison. Second render selected; `DONE` (lines 3–15). | Technical success; clipping diagnosis and improvement unverified. |
| **S0227** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C2/development/commons_187101683/trajectory.jsonl` | Sofa-room-interpreted build rendered; student revised camera, table, foliage and curtain. Second render selected; `DONE` (lines 3–15). | Technical success; correspondence and improvement unknown. |
| **S0228** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C1/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl` | Student CLI call timed out before a returned program, after about 300 seconds (lines 1–4). | Interrupted; no execution or render. Not evidence of an empty patch or algorithmic failure. |
| **S0229** `scene_rsi_v2_1/C1/development/commons_187101683/trajectory.jsonl` | Substantial scene program attempted; Blender timed out after about 481 seconds, with no image (lines 3–5). | Interrupted execution; cause and scene quality unknown. |
| **S0230** `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_189918915/trajectory.jsonl` | Nonempty warehouse-interpreted program attempted; execution timed out after about 478 seconds, with no image (lines 3–5). | Interrupted execution, not demonstrated algorithm failure. |
| **S0231** `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_80372956/trajectory.jsonl` | Nonempty ceiling/chandelier-interpreted program attempted; execution timed out after about 516 seconds, with no image (lines 3–5). | Interrupted execution; no visual review or correction shown. |
| **S0232** `fixed_h0/H0/selection/commons_194983350/trajectory.jsonl` | Nonempty café-interpreted program attempted; first execution timed out after about 316 seconds, with no image (lines 3–5). | Interrupted execution; no second execution recorded. |
| **S0233** `fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_187101683/trajectory.jsonl` | First execution failed because `scene.world` was `None`; the student received the traceback, revised initialization and camera settings, and reran successfully. Render selected and `DONE` returned (lines 3–14). | Observed technical failure and recovery; visual quality unknown. |

## Comparison and interpretation

**Successful execution is not established reconstruction success.** S0224–S0227 each show a completed first render, a student comparison, an executed revision and a selected second render. Their student diagnoses were specific: for example, S0225 reported reversed chandelier spokes and washed-out brass, whereas S0226 reported oversized foreground objects and clipping (respective lines 7–12). The changes were not empty patches. Yet the audits cannot independently see the images or establish object coverage, physical contacts, material appearance, pose, lighting, framing, or whether either revision improved fidelity. `ok: true`, selection and `DONE` establish the recorded workflow status, not visual acceptance by an independent evaluator.

**Failure and interruption are distinct.** S0233’s first run produced a specific initialization traceback, and its second run succeeded after a corresponding world-creation edit; its simultaneous camera changes are not validated by that recovery (lines 5–10). In contrast, S0229–S0232 have `ok: false`, empty logs and null images after timeouts. They show submitted programs and interrupted executions, not identified faulty reconstruction algorithms or verified partial scenes. S0228 stopped earlier, at the student CLI call, with no returned program. No permission denial or branch stop is reported in these files; the CLI timeout should not be recast as either. No verified empty patch is shown.

The same named image identifiers occur across conditions—for example, S0224/S0230, S0225/S0231, S0226/S0228/S0232, and S0227/S0229/S0233. These are separate recorded attempts on associated identifiers, not independent source images. Their differing outcomes are useful counterexamples to a blanket claim that a particular task always renders or always times out, but they do not establish causal superiority of any condition. File counts, including any copies, are not counts of independent trials.

## Advice, adoption, and transferable limits

All ten files are student trajectories. No teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is recorded in them; consequently teacher advice availability, actual receipt and adoption are not established. The rendered comparisons supplied to S0224–S0227 were runner feedback, not evidence of a teacher intervention. Their diagnoses and subsequent code changes are visible student actions. S0233 likewise acted on a runner traceback, not documented teacher advice. No teacher-driven update or teacher acceptance is evidenced, and independent visual quality remains unknown.

Across these attempts, the transferable distinction is between an inspectable program, a completed render, a student’s diagnosis, an executed change, and independently verified fidelity. Named hierarchies and coordinates document intended editable parts and relationships, but do not prove contact or image correspondence. S0227’s coordinated table and object offsets are an observed task-specific change, not proof of correct connections (lines 9–10). Simultaneous camera, geometry, material and lighting edits also prevent attribution of any unobserved improvement to one change.

The reported warehouse color-node explanation, chandelier orientation, café framing and sofa/curtain diagnoses are hypotheses grounded in students’ own reviews, not independently established defects. Similarly, dense geometry or render settings might have contributed to a timeout, but the empty logs do not identify its cause. Missing formal visual scores are unknown, and old model cost cannot be recovered from their absence. This report makes no new solution, feedback, skill, or causal-superiority claim.
